title: PetroPoin earn rate — per-litre margin headroom test
prompt:
You are Citra Widyastuti, Analyst at Aurelian & Co., PetroNusa engagement (loyalty workstream). It is early August 2025. The loyalty current-state assessment was accepted at SteerCo 4 in June; the working summary, the handoff note and the client's programme documentation are all in the project folder, along with the CRM and transaction extracts.

Marcus Whelan writes:

---
Subject: Earn rate — the per-litre arithmetic, before SteerCo 5

Citra,

Mei-Ling's line to the steering group was that customers love points, so double the earn rate. Bambang is half-persuaded. Before we argue about tiers and cashback I want the narrow question answered properly: what does the earn actually cost us on the litre that earns it, and is there room under the fuel margin to double it.

So, per litre of fuel, on the current indicative pump price and fuel gross margin in the research file:

1. what the programme is issuing today per litre;
2. what that costs us, on an expected basis, per litre;
3. that cost against the fuel gross margin on the same litre;
4. what is left of the fuel gross margin per litre if the earn is doubled as proposed;
5. the most we could issue per litre and still respect Bambang's constraint, which is that reward cost on the earning litre must not exceed one fifth of the fuel gross margin on that litre.

Do not rely on any single document's description of the mechanic — reconcile what the programme says it does with what its records show it doing, and be explicit in the memo about which reading each number sits on. Wallet sourcing stays with Hendra's team; stay in our lane.

Thanks, Marcus
---

Deliverables: a headroom model in Excel with the per-litre build visible, and a short memo. Save them as `petropoin_earn_rate_headroom_model.xlsx` and `petropoin_earn_rate_headroom_memo.docx` in your output directory.

checks.description: Points per litre evidenced in the FY2024 transaction extract: 122 points on 12.2 litres = 10 points per litre, consistent across all fuel rows carrying points.

refs.quote: the points column is exactly ten times the litres column

checks.report_ask: Report the number of points the programme is currently issuing per litre of fuel.

decoy.description: Taking the earn rate as documented in the client-facing programme overview.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Expected reward cost per earning litre = 10 points x (5 x 13,500 / 500) x (1 - 0.382) = 834.3 SRP per litre.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

checks.report_ask: Report the reward cost PetroNusa expects to bear per litre of fuel earned on, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Costing the documented one-point-per-litre rule instead of the rate the records show.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Expected reward cost per earning litre (834.3 SRP) as a percentage of fuel gross margin per litre (513 SRP) = 162.63%.
checks.report_ask: Report the reward cost per earning litre as a percentage of the fuel gross margin on that same litre.

decoy.description: Costing points at full face redemption value with no breakage allowance.

checks.description: Fuel gross margin per litre left after reward cost if the earn rate is doubled = 513 - 2 x 834.3 = -1,155.6 SRP per litre.
checks.report_ask: Report the fuel gross margin remaining per litre after reward cost if the earn rate is doubled as proposed, in SRP per litre.

decoy.description: Doubling the documented one-point-per-litre rule rather than the earn the records show.

refs.name: documented_rule
refs.quote: Members earn 1 PetroPoin point for every litre of fuel purchased at a participating station

checks.description: Maximum points per litre within a cap of one fifth of fuel gross margin = 0.2 x 513 / (135 x 0.618) = 1.2298 points per litre.

refs.name: redemption_rule
refs.quote: 500 points redeemed at any participating station in exchange for 5 litres of fuel

checks.report_ask: Report the maximum number of points per litre the programme can issue while respecting the margin constraint set out in the brief.

decoy.description: Sizing the cap on full face redemption value with no breakage allowance.

difficulty_rationale: The client's Programme Overview states one point per litre; every fuel row in the FY2024 transaction extract that carries points shows points at exactly ten times litres, and the handoff note flags the mechanic as unresolved and load-bearing for any earn-rate change. Costing the earn also requires the 500-points-for-5-litres redemption rule against pump price (135 SRP per point) and the approved 38.2% breakage rather than the superseded ~45% in the client pack. The obvious path (documented 1 point per litre, or face value with no breakage) produces a cost an order of magnitude too small and makes doubling the earn look affordable, when on the recorded basis the earn already exceeds the entire fuel gross margin on the litre.

--- Output format requirement (machine-graded) ---
Alongside your deliverable(s), write a `report.json` in your output directory with

- `result_01` — Report the number of points the programme is currently issuing per litre of fuel. (unit: points per litre)
- `result_02` — Report the reward cost PetroNusa expects to bear per litre of fuel earned on, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_03` — Report the reward cost per earning litre as a percentage of the fuel gross margin on that same litre. (unit: pct)
- `result_04` — Report the fuel gross margin remaining per litre after reward cost if the earn rate is doubled as proposed, in SRP per litre. (unit: SRP per litre)
- `result_05` — Report the maximum number of points per litre the programme can issue while respecting the margin constraint set out in the brief. (unit: points per litre)

Your work is graded programmatically from `report.json` and the deliverable files.
A key that is missing, renamed, wrapped in a container, or given as prose scores zero.
